spec.name: distill_pilot_50_vs_800
spec.question: Do stronger MCTS targets transfer through distillation into a fixed 172k student? Arms are 50-sim and 800-sim teachers over IDENTICAL positions.
spec.why_these_arms: RESULT_TEACHER_SIM_LADDER.md measured +0.019 strength per doubling, so the 800-vs-200 teacher gap (~4 pts) sits under the ~0.05 panel floor. 50-vs-800 (~17 pts) is the only contrast with adequate signal. A 200 arm is deliberately NOT generated yet; it is a curve-shape arm for later.

corpus.sampling: uniform random, natural phase distribution (NOT stratified)
corpus.policy_target: full MCTS visit distribution (not top move)
corpus.value_target: original corpus outcome z, IDENTICAL across arms

student.pairing: For each seed the two arms share init weights AND batch order; only the policy targets differ. Three seeds per arm so training variance is measured, not assumed.

evaluation.primary: student_800 vs student_50 head to head
evaluation.primary_note: Paired openings, colors swapped. Extend beyond 800 only if the CI still materially overlaps 0.5. 800 games is the known resolution scale from the teacher ladder, where neither 400-game block separated alone.
evaluation.elo: NOT a primary result; internal Elo is self-play inflated
evaluation.explicitly_not_required: The student gap need NOT approach the teacher's ~17-point gap. The question is whether stronger targets transfer AT ALL and how much survives compression.

secondary: breakout by phase, branching factor, tactical status, teacher value gap

whether gains concentrate where adjudication says the 800-sim move is better -- CAVEAT: RESULT_SEARCH_DISAGREEMENT.md found the adjudicator cannot resolve this (independent referee at chance, same-net signals contradictory), so treat this item as exploratory, not confirmatory

decision_rules.clear_win: run the full equal-example experiment; add 200 as a curve arm
decision_rules.directional_unresolved: add evaluation games first, do NOT regenerate corpora
decision_rules.flat_across_seeds: investigate student capacity, target weighting, optimization
decision_rules.reversal: check whether higher-sim policies are softer/noisier/harder to fit for a fixed student
